definition: Publication acknowledgement(s) for the published dataset.
Mechanism by which the project will be made avilable.
Is the project open or restricted?
Unique identifier for the project.
Description of whether the project submission is complete or still in progress.
The citation for the published dataset.
The name of the organization or individual that the contributed dataset belongs to.
A brief, free-text description of the data files and associated metadata provided for this dataset.
A URL or DOI for the source of the dataset or the contributing organization's website.
The date or date range in which the project data was collected.
The dbgap accession number provided for the project.
The primary type of disease studied in this dataset, if applicable.
UUID for the project.
Tracks a Project's intended release date.
The investigator's affiliation with respect to a research institution.
Name of the principal investigator for the project.
The license under which the dataset has been published.
Indicates whether the dataset has longitudinal or time-series data.
Display name/brief description for the project.
The primary body site studied in this dataset.
The program to which the project belongs.
The major or main publication(s) associated with the data itself or with the publication that published the dataset.
A project can only be released by the user when `releasable` is true.

To release a project is to tell the GDC to include all submitted
entities in the next GDC index.

If the dataset is related to a research study, provide a brief, free-text description or abstract of the study being performed, for example, the hypothesis being tested and a very brief description of the materials, methods and results.
A summary of the goals of the research or a general description of the research's relationship to a clinical application.
The general objective of the research; what the researchers hope to discover or determine.
A high level description of the setup used to achieve the research objectives.

The possible states a project can be in. All but 'open' are
equivalent to some type of locked state.
The ID of the source providing support/grant resources.
The name of source providing support/grant resources.
